A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RiboFlow model and RiboBind dataset. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original unconditional and ligand-conditioned RNA generation experiments, ablations, few-shot evaluations, sampling-time measurements, and design case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation experiments and adds structural-holdout results, long-RNA evaluations, and comparisons using different backbone atoms.

M1.justification: The flow objectives, torsion predictor, ligand-conditioned IPA module, dynamic cropping, and RiboFlow-T coordinate-centering procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 moves to the appendix without procedural changes. Renaming RiboFlow-Structure and RiboFlow-Codesign does not establish a changed model.

E1.justification: Section 8.3 adds RNA generation-quality evaluation at lengths 200–450, extending beyond v1's 50–150 quality evaluations and timing tests through approximately 300 nucleotides. RNAsolo, RiboBind, and the ligand-structure and SMILES tasks remain. PDBBind and RNAmigos2 are discussed comparatively, not introduced as new model benchmarks.

E2.justification: The local-geometry comparison adds RNA-FrameFlow-R alongside RiboFlow and real structures in Figure 8; v1 Appendix B.2 described only RiboFlow-Codesign versus real structures. The principal generation comparator sets remain matched, including RiboFlow-Structure renamed RNA-FrameFlow-R. GerNA-Bind is an evaluation scorer, not a new generation baseline.

E3.justification: v3 adds a structural split with 249 training and 28 test classes and revises the sequence/few-shot split descriptions, replacing v1's blanket ligand-exclusion assertion. Reported generation counts increase from 50 to 100 for unconditional and ligand-structure experiments, and from 50 to 200 per length for SMILES experiments. GNINA affinity/pose metrics are replaced by GerNA scores, and docking is attributed to AutoDock Vina. New long-RNA and multi-atom evaluations introduce additional protocols. These are documented setting changes, not proof that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test long-sequence generalization, sensitivity to C3'/C4'/C5' atom selection, and performance under structural holdout. Local-geometry analysis also becomes an explicit model comparison. These substantially broaden validation beyond v1's pretraining, cropping, centering, and case-study analyses. The sampling-time plot already existed in v1; its expanded discussion is not a new timing experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies independent-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance-testing procedures. The new long-RNA boxplots extend sample-distribution reporting already present in v1's violin plots. Increased generated-sample counts are protocol changes, not evidence of additional independent runs.

E6.justification: Reported unconditional RiboFlow validity changes from 37.0/34.3 to 34.7/31.9 at 50/100 sampling steps. Table 2's +PRE sampled-length validity changes from 35.8 to 25.9, while Table 3's +PRE sequence recovery/RMSD changes from 47.4/5.94 to 33.4/9.43. These are not controlled performance declines because reported protocols also change. v3 adds GerNA, structural-holdout, long-RNA, and atom-wise results, while removing few-shot validity/diversity/novelty entries and tabulated GNINA affinity/pose scores.

T1.justification: The probabilistic formulation, interpolation equations, losses, and continuous-flow derivation remain mathematically unchanged. v3 numbers an already-present translation-loss expression and renumbers the appendix equations. The additional empirical metric explanations do not introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The introduction and main dataset description soften RiboBind's characterization from the largest standardized benchmark to a large benchmark, although Appendix 7.1 retains the largest-dataset claim. The central claims about ligand-conditioned co-design, structural validity, and binding performance remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive applicability limits: poorer long-RNA generation, uncertainty from using RhoFold beyond its validated length range, and the absence of wet-lab binding validation. It also proposes an explanation for stronger predicted affinities with SMILES-derived conformers and interprets sampling-cost scaling. These materially expand the qualifications and mechanisms discussed in v1.

D1.justification: v3 documents the 4.3-angstrom scRMSD validity cutoff, multi-atom evaluation details, RTX 4090 memory constraints, and a GerNA-Bind access link. The architecture hyperparameters, four-A100 pretraining setup, approximate training time, and inference pseudocode were already supplied in v1 and are largely retained or relocated.

R1.justification: New Section 7.2 positions RiboBind relative to PDBBind and RNAmigos2 through reported dataset overlap and distinctions between experimental structures and synthetic docking data. References to those datasets, GerNA-Bind, and AutoDock Vina are added, while the GNINA evaluation reference is removed. The main related-work narrative remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most abstract, introduction, method, and conclusion prose is retained. Changes include the shortened title, author information, model terminology, localized experimental rewrites, an appendix contents list, and reorganization of inference, implementation, and impact material. The extensive new scientific material does not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Table 2 and the few-shot table change column structure; new structural-holdout and atom-wise tables and a length-evaluation plot are added. Local-geometry plots expand, the timing plot moves to the appendix, and the pretraining curve disappears while its tabulated results remain.

improvement.justification: Structural-holdout results, atom-choice checks, and long-RNA failure analysis make generalization and applicability more assessable than in v1. Explicit acknowledgment that binding predictions lack wet-lab validation also improves the paper's qualifications. The net gain is limited by removal of few-shot structural-quality results and inconsistent evaluation documentation: AutoDock Vina replaces GNINA in the stated pipeline, but GNINA descriptions and pose-score plots remain, including figures whose revised captions mention only Vina.
